Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le \alpha<1$, we construct a $C^{1,\alpha}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. In step-2 Carnot groups, we show that every $C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension less than or equal to $q-\frac{1+\alpha}2$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. This upper bound is actually attained by the $C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurfaces of our construction, hence their Euclidean Hausdorff dimension is maximal. As a technical result of independent interest, we show that the implicit function associated with a $C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurface is $\frac{1+\alpha}2$-Euclidean Hölder continuous, with $0\le\alpha\le 1$. In particular, $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurfaces in step-2 Carnot groups are rectifiable in the classical sense, therefore the range of unrectifiability $0\le \alpha<1$ is sharp. We also prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. The previous results extend the seminal work of Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group and settle a question concerning the singular surface they constructed, by proving that its $\frac52$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure is zero.

papers.title: Explicit counterexamples to Frank-Loss optimizer conjectures for critical Dirac and vector Sobolev inequalities
papers.abstract: Frank and Loss proposed critical Sobolev inequalities for the Dirac operator and for vector fields. They conjectured optimality of their spinorial family and wrote that it is conceivable that the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau potential is an optimizer. Wang and Zhang recently disproved both optimizer claims using direct comparison and instability arguments. We compute closed-form quotients for two elementary families of explicit competitors with strictly smaller quotients. For every $d\geq2$, the spinorial competitor is a constant spinor multiplied by a scalar Aubin-Talenti optimizer. For every $d\geq3$, the vector competitor is the planar azimuthal field \[ A_d(x)=\frac{d}{(1+\lvert x\rvert^2)^2} (-x_2,x_1,0,\ldots,0). \] It lies in the nonlinear gauge and its quotient is computed in closed form. For every odd $d\geq3$, it gives an explicit proof of nonoptimality of the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau-Dunne-Min potential. In dimension three, this field is a specific member of the competitor family of Wang and Zhang: it is a linear combination of the Loss-Yau potential and its reflected twin. Its axisymmetry gives a negative answer to their question about minimization within the $\mathrm{SO}(2)\times 1$-invariant class.

papers.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
papers.abstract: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

Little Red Dots as Shock-Powered High-Energy Neutrino Sources
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, high-redshift sources whose physical nature remains uncertain. Their optical spectra motivate a scenario in which their emission may be powered by shocks interacting with dense surrounding material. We investigate whether such interactions can power LRDs and contribute to the diffuse high-energy neutrino intensity measured by IceCube. In our simplified model, a fast central-engine outflow drives a shock through stationary or slow outflowing material, followed by a prescribed quasi-stationary interaction near the LRD photosphere. We consider the time-averaged neutrino emission from shock-active LRDs without requiring a single shock to persist throughout the LRD lifetime. We explore parameter ranges motivated by the observed and inferred properties of LRDs, finding solutions with shock luminosities 2.0e43 < L_s < 3.5e44 erg/s. Using an analytical framework for cosmic-ray acceleration and hadronic interactions in dense shock environments, we calculate the resulting high-energy neutrino emission and integrate it over the cosmological LRD population. For our fiducial cosmic-ray parameters, the average predicted contribution below 2e5 GeV increases from 0.2% for the lowest-luminosity quintile to 2% for the highest-luminosity quintile, while an illustrative higher-efficiency case reaches 13% of the IceCube diffuse neutrino intensity. These estimates assume all observed LRDs are shock-active. A smaller active fraction or a reduced covering factor would decrease the predicted intensity, whereas survey incompleteness could increase it. Improved models and population synthesis are needed to constrain the total LRD contribution.

Gravitational Wave Modeling of White-Dwarf--Compact-Object Binaries and Observational Outlook
papers.abstract: Binaries consisting of a white dwarf and a compact object (neutron stars, black holes, or sub-solar-mass compact objects) display unique orbital evolution and gravitational wave signals. We investigate the end stages of these systems by developing a novel integrator implementing mass transfer and 2.5-order Post-Newtonian kinematics. White-dwarf--compact-object binaries are subject to two phases: a slow inspiral during which binary evolution is dominated by weak-gravity radiation reaction and a quicker "outspiral" dominated by mass transfer. These systems have unique gravitational waveforms with several characteristic features including an accumulation of signal near the maximum cutoff frequency set by the transition between in- and outspiral. We investigate trends in gravitational wave parameters based on component masses. In particular, maximum cutoff frequency depends strongly on white dwarf mass and compactness. It is unlikely that extragalactic binaries will be measured by LISA or current or future terrestrial detectors. However, white-dwarf--compact-object binary end stages will be an important source for future decihertz detectors such as DECIGO and LGWA: The final inspiral of tens of white-dwarf--neutron-star binaries will be detected annually by LGWA, and millions of inspirals along with thousands of outspirals will be detected by DECIGO. The ultimate fates of these binaries are diverse and dependent upon the intricacies of angular momentum loss. In particular, we show that white dwarfs with partners of sufficiently low/high mass can end their lives in mergers, while white dwarfs do not enter contact with partners of intermediate mass. The highest frequencies produced by white-dwarf--compact-object binaries in our tests are 10--20 Hz--incapable of mimicking sub-solar-mass compact object signals in terrestrial detectors or explaining S251112cm-like signals.

Students' Validation Criteria for AI-Generated Physics Solutions
papers.abstract: A physics solution can be clear without being valid. This distinction becomes important when students read AI-generated solutions that appear coherent but still require physical and mathematical checking. We examined how pre-service physics teachers in a calculus-based introductory electromagnetism course evaluated AI-generated solutions to a charged-rod electric-field problem after attempting the problem themselves. Although the AI-generated solutions analyzed were correct, no student accepted a response as valid after a first reading. Students who had solved the problem fully or in part could examine the responses using physical and mathematical criteria, while others withheld acceptance because they could not follow the mathematical development. These results suggest that, in physics instruction, AI-generated solutions should be treated less as answers to be accepted or rejected and more as worked-out responses that students learn to reconstruct, question, and test.

papers.title: Beyond the probabilistic scaling for NLS on the ball
papers.abstract: We construct probabilistic strong solutions to the cubic Schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional ball with radial initial data, which is a significant improvement of a result by Bourgain--Bulut. These solutions lie in the supercritical regime with respect to the probabilistic scaling introduced by Deng--Nahmod--Yue. We achieve this result through gauge transformations, without renormalization, combined with a refined modulation analysis using random averaging operators.

A Closer Look on the Influence of Constraints Upon the Optimization of the Nonadditive Entropic Functional $S_{q}$
papers.abstract: The canonical distribution is obtained by maximizing the Boltzmann-Gibbs-von Neumann-Shannon entropy $S_{BG}(p)=k\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}\ln 1/p_{i}$ constrained to $\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}=1$ and $\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}\,e_{i}=U$, $e_{1}\leq\ldots\leq e_{W}$ being the energies of the $W$ possible states and $U\in[e_{1},e_{W}]$ their mean value. We revisit a generalized version of this optimization problem grounded in the nonadditive entropy $S_{q}(p)=k\,(\sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}^{q}-1)/(1-q)$ (frequently, though not necessarily, $q\in(0,1)$; $S_1=S_{BG}$), and the constraint $\sum^{W}_{i=1} p_{i}^{q^{\prime}}e_{i} / \sum^{W}_{i=1}p_{i}^{q^{\prime}}=U$, $q^{\prime}>0$. Sufficient conditions for existence, strict positivity, and uniqueness of solutions are derived, along with a theorem that enables their closed-form calculation. We apply these results to deepen the understanding of the two standard cases in the literature ($q^{\prime}=1$ and $q^{\prime}=q$), as well as of a new one ($q^{\prime}=2-q$). We prove that these standard cases are the only ones yielding optimizing probability distributions of $q$-exponential form. Furthermore, we define an effective temperature $T_{q,q^{\prime}}$ through a Clausius-like relation $1/T_{q,q^{\prime}}=\partial S_{q} / \partial U$ and derive a Helmholtz-like energy $F_{q,q^{\prime}}=U-T_{q,q^{\prime}}S_{q}$, with the former grounding the validity of the $0^{\textrm{th}}$ Principle of Thermodynamics within this generalized statistical mechanics. Finally, we show that the case with a linear constraint (i.e., $q^{\prime}=1$) with $q\in(0,1)$ (i) preserves the Third Law of Thermodynamics; (ii) can be used to model classical many-body Hamiltonian systems with arbitrarily-ranged interactions; and (iii) resembles features of low-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems at the edge of chaos.

papers.title: Scalable spin-nematic squeezing in multi-level dipole-interacting Rydberg atom arrays
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical generation of metrologically useful entanglement in arrays of three-level (spin-1) systems coupled by spin-exchange interactions, as realized by dipole-interacting Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers. We quantify the metrological gain by a generalized squeezing parameter optimized over all linear $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ phase generators and readout observables. For equal exchange couplings on the two transitions, the dynamics reduces to one-axis twisting (OAT) of an effective two-level system. Away from this point, the full three-level structure provides a genuine advantage. For all-to-all couplings, the optimal squeezing at $N=4000$ exceeds the OAT value by a factor of 3.6, with a fitted scaling exponent of $0.93$ compared with $0.69$ for OAT over $100\le N\le4000$. For two-dimensional dipolar arrays, exact and tensor-network simulations up to $N=49$ show that the optimal three-level protocol outperforms the effective spin-1/2 dynamics, with a gain that increases with system size, and semiclassical simulations show that squeezing continues to grow up to $N=10^4$. Crucially, our results demonstrate a real advantage of utilizing the full three-level $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ structure of the spin-1 system over $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ type one-axis twisting dynamics. Our results extend interaction-driven scalable squeezing beyond the well-studied qubit setting to spin-exchange-coupled qudits with dipolar interactions, and can be realized in current Rydberg tweezer experiments.

papers.title: Untrained CNNs Exceed Backpropagation in V1 Alignment at High Evaluation Resolution: A Systematic RSA Comparison of Four Learning Rules Against Human fMRI
Exact solution of two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on a strip
papers.abstract: We analyze the two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on an infinite strip (product of a finite interval with the infinite line, corresponding to ``time"). The theory has only boundary degrees of freedom. Its phase space is the cotangent bundle to the group manifold of $SL(2,\mathbf{R})$, subject to a (first-class) constraint quadratic in the momenta. With the simplest choice of boundary Hamiltonian, namely $H = 0$, the theory is shown to describe geodesics on the group manifold of $SL(2,\mathbf{R})$, with a ``mass" determined by the Palatini Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant. Other choices of boundary Hamiltonians compatible with gauge invariance are also possible. The symmetry group contains (left and right) group translations on $SL(2,\mathbf{R})$. These are ``boundary symmetries" from the bulk point of view, one copy acting on one end of the interval, the other copy acting on the other end. Comments on the quantum theory are also given.

papers.title: A Geometric Framework for Conditional Stability in Overdetermined Elliptic Problems
papers.abstract: We present a geometric framework for studying stability and symmetry in overdetermined elliptic boundary value problems. The approach is based on a normal radial parametrization of domains with respect to a strictly convex core $C$. We establish unconditional qualitative stability for second and fourth-order problems (Serrin and Bennett--Dalmasso). We then derive conditional quantitative stability estimates assuming a residual estimate for the tangential component. The method does not rely on moving planes or the maximum principle. The quantitative results are conditional upon a sufficient analytical assumption that we carefully formulate, including a control of the tangential gradient; we verify this assumption in two model cases. The quantitative results are stated and proved in the model case $C=\{0\}$; the general strictly convex core is discussed in Remark and left for future work.

papers.title: Blown-up singular Riemannian foliations
papers.abstract: We study the effect of projective blow-ups on the leaf closures and basic cohomology of singular Riemannian foliations. For a foliation with smooth Molino sheaf on a compact manifold, we show that the Molino sheaf of the blow-up is the inverse image of the original sheaf under blow-down. In particular, desingularization preserves the Killing property and the structural Lie algebra. We obtain a closedness criterion in terms of the Euler characteristics of the ambient manifold and the blow-up centers, assuming finite fundamental group and singular strata of codimension at least three. For singular Killing foliations on compact manifolds, we approximate the space of leaf closures in Gromov--Hausdorff distance by Riemannian orbifolds whose dimension equals the codimension of the foliation. Finally, relative basic cohomology gives a long exact sequence relating the original foliation, its blow-up, and their restrictions to the center and the exceptional divisor.

papers.title: Generalized Boltzmann-Gibbs Distributions and the Electronic Partition Function Paradox
papers.abstract: The maximization of the nonadditive entropic functional $S_{q}(p)=k\sum_{i}p_{i}\ln_{q}(1/p_{i})$, $q\in(0,1)$, under a linear mean-energy constraint, i.e., the best-behaved case from Dognini and Tsallis (2026), is used to derive generalizations of the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution for physical systems whose description requires a limiting process over the energy spectrum: the hydrogen atom in free space; an energy spectrum that uniformly approaches a continuous, unbounded limit with a common degeneracy; the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of velocities; the harmonic oscillator; and the one-dimensional box. For the hydrogen atom with mean energy $U\in[0,e_{ion}]$, the limiting optimal distribution is a two-tier one, concentrated on the ground level and on the ionization threshold, with weights $1-U/e_{ion}$ and $U/e_{ion}$ for every $q\in(0,1)$, and the temperature rescaled by $\ln_{q}W$ is finite and given by $T_{q,s}=T_{ion}(U/e_{ion})^{1-q}$, with $T_{ion}=e_{ion}/kq$. This circumvents the Electronic Partition Function Paradox and yields a family of well-defined thermodynamic behaviors.

papers.title: SURFing to the Fundamental Limit of Jet Tagging
On a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture via categorical representations
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a complex reductive group. For a smooth affine spherical $G$-variety $X$ such that the stabilizer of a point in the $B$-orbit under the $B$-action be connected, assume that the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi-Sakellaridis-Venkatesh (BZSV) for $X$ holds. We establish a spectral description of a full subcategory of Iwahori equivariant coherent D-modules on $LX$ in terms of the relative Langlands dual of $X$, confirming a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture proposed by Devalapurkar.

papers.title: Learning Greens Operators through Hierarchical Neural Networks Inspired by the Fast Multipole Method
Differentiable-by-design Nonlinear Optimization for Model Predictive Control
Asymptotic analysis on narrow tubes: narrow escape problems and diffusion processes
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a diffusion process in a narrow tubular domain with reflecting boundary conditions, where the geometry serves as a singular perturbation of an underlying graph in $\mathbb{R}^2$ or $\mathbb{R}^3$. The construction incorporates distinct scaling regimes in the neighborhoods of the graph's vertices and edges. We show that, in the limit, the projected process converges weakly to a diffusion process on the graph, with gluing conditions at the vertices that depend on the relative scales of the neighborhoods. Our analysis relies on a detailed understanding of the narrow escape problem in domains with bottlenecks. In particular, we rigorously derive the asymptotic behavior of the expected escape time, establish the asymptotic exponential distribution of escape times and obtain exit place estimates, results that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Say It Another Way: Auditing LLMs with a User-Grounded Automated Paraphrasing Framework
Relativistic Navier-Stokes description of the quark-gluon plasma radial flow
papers.abstract: Using relativistic Navier-Stokes in the well-posed Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) formulation, with a QCD equation of state and transport coefficients, we perform simulations that describe the radial flow in central Pb-Pb collisions measured at the LHC, providing a proof of principle for its viability in heavy-ion phenomenology. We identify causal frames that retain the Landau-frame interpretation, and verify frame robustness. Müller-Israel-Stewart simulations with identical input show large second-order effects, exceeding the frame dependence of relativistic Navier-Stokes, as well as causality violations.

papers.title: NS-Gym: A Comprehensive and Open-Source Simulation Framework for Non-Stationary Markov Decision Processes
Cohomological VC-density: Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: The concept of Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) density is pivotal across various mathematical fields, including discrete geometry, probability theory and model theory. In this paper, we introduce a topological generalization of VC-density. Let $Y$ be a topological space and $\mathcal{X}$ a family of closed subspaces of $Y$. For each $p \geq 0$, we define a number, $\mathrm{vcd}^{p}_{\mathcal{X}}$, which we refer to as the degree $p$ VC-density of the family $\mathcal{X}$. The classical notion of VC-density within this topological framework can be recovered by setting $p=0$. Our definition of degree $p$ VC-density extends to higher orders as well. For $p \geq 0$, $q \geq 1$, we define the degree $p$, order $q$ VC density $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$ of $\mathcal{X}$, which recovers Shelah's notion of higher order VC-density for $q$-dependent families when $p=0$. Our definition introduces a completely new notion when $p > 0$. We examine the properties of $\mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p$ (as well as $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$) when the families $\mathcal{X}$ are definable in structures with some underlying topology (for instance, the Euclidean topology for o-minimal structures over $\mathbb{R}$, the analytic topology over $\mathbb{C}$, or the étale site for schemes over arbitrary algebraically closed fields). Our main result establishes that in any model of these theories \[ \mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p \leq (p+1) \dim X, \] and more generally for any $q \geq 1$ \[ \mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}} \leq (p+q) \dim X. \] We give examples to show that our bounds are optimal. We also present combinatorial applications of our higher-degree VC-density bounds, deriving higher degree topological analogs of well-known results such as the existence of $\varepsilon$-nets and the fractional Helly theorem.

papers.title: On completed homology and a conjecture of Venkatesh
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a CM field and $\Pi$ a regular algebraic cuspidal cohomological representation of $\mathbf{G}=\operatorname{PGL}_2/F$. A conjecture of Venkatesh describes the structure of the contribution of $\Pi$ to the homology of the locally symmetric spaces associated to $\mathbf{G}$. We investigate this conjecture in the setting of $p$-adic homology with $p$ a totally split prime. Along the way, we elaborate on the relations between Venkatesh's conjecture and completed homology, the Taylor-Wiles method and the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence. Our main result is a `big $R=T$' theorem in characteristic 0, from which we deduce a variant of the $p$-adic realisation of Venkatesh's conjecture, conditional on various natural conjectures and technical assumptions.
